s.g: A visual representation of an area, whether real or imaginary, showing the relative positions of places and other features.
s.x: a map of Australia, a map of Lilliput

s.g: A graphical or logical representation of any structure or system, showing the positions of or relationships between its components.
s.x: a map of the Earth's magnetic field

s.g: (mathematics) A function, especially a function satisfying a certain property (e.g. continuity, linearity, etc.; see Usage notes).
(entomology) Any of various nymphalid butterflies of the genera Araschnia (especially, Araschnia levana) and Cyrestis, having map-like markings on the wings.
(board games, video games) An imaginary or fictional area, often predefined and confined, where a game or a session thereof takes place.
s.x: I don't want to play this map again!

s.g: (transitive) To represent by means of a map.
s.x: This large atlas maps the whole world in very great detail.

s.g: (transitive) To create a map of; to examine or survey in order to gather information for a map.
s.x: The team is mapping the route of the new railway line.

s.g: (intransitive, followed by a "to" phrase) To have a direct relationship; to correspond.
s.x: This doesn't map to my understanding of how things should work.

s.g: (transitive, followed by a "to" phrase) To create a direct relationship to; to create a correspondence with.
s.x: Map "volume down" to the F2 key.

s.g: (mathematics, transitive, followed by a "to" phrase) To act as a function on something, taking it to something else.
(slang, neologism) a non-binary parent.
Any member of any species of genus Acer, characterized by (usually) palmate, five-lobed leaves and winged seeds, and often grown for syrup or wood

(countable, UK) A small tree (Acer campestre), known as the common maple, field maple, or hedge maple, which has palmate leaves with five lobes and winged seeds, and is chiefly native to East Asia, Europe, North Africa, and North America.

(countable) Often preceded by a descriptive word: a tree of the genus Acer; especially the sugar maple (Acer saccharum) native to North America which has brightly colored autumn foliage and is the primary source of maple syrup.
(countable) Chiefly preceded by a descriptive word: a tree of a genus other than Acer which has an appearance or wood similar to an Acer tree.
(uncountable) Wood of an Acer tree, valued for its attractive appearance and hardness; also, similar wood from a tree of a genus other than Acer; (countable) a particular type of such wood.
s.x: This table is made of maple and also has some fruitwood inlays.

Of the flavour of, or made with, maple syrup.
(New Zealand, archaic) Synonym of mapau (“any of several trees of New Zealand, especially in the genus Myrsine”).
A person who makes maps.
Cartography, the making of maps and charts.
On Haiti, the kapok tree, Ceiba pentandra.

s.g: Able to be represented by a map.
s.x: Satellite imagery has made many inaccessible areas much more mappable.

s.g: Able to be associated with something else by means of a mapping.
s.x: Computers on the Internet are mappable to IP addresses.

s.g: Having been mapped; (graphic design) having had a map projected onto its surface.

mapped.f: simple past and past participle of map

s.g: One who produces a map.
(video games) A designer of levels for video games.
(computing, electronics) A software or hardware component that performs a mapping.
The process of making maps.
(biology) The process of locating genes on a chromosome.
(computing) Assigning a PC to a shared drive or printer port on a network.
(mathematics) A function that maps every element of a given mathematical structure (eg: a set) to a unique element of another structure; a correspondence.
(object-oriented programming) conversion of data types between incompatible type systems.
